name: Schedule3D
tagline: Turns a construction schedule (P6 XML, XER, XLSX, CSV) into an evidence-linked 3D and 4D model of the facility.
problem: Project schedules hold thousands of activities but nobody can see the plant they describe. Schedule3D reads every activity and builds a schematic 3D model with a timeline, so planners, project controls and stakeholders can watch the build sequence and check what each element is based on. It is local-first, so sensitive schedules stay on the machine.
how: Upload one or more schedules (XER, P6 XML, XLSX, CSV or TSV), optionally with project documents as evidence.
Unknown spreadsheet headings open a column mapping screen where you map source columns to activity ID, name, WBS and dates.
The backend parses each file separately and keeps every project with its own IDs and dates; multi-project sources open a project chooser or programme mode.
A deterministic classifier recognises the industry and activity types and places representative elements on a labelled schematic grid.
The 3D viewer plays the schedule as a 4D sequence, and every element links back to its supporting activities, dates and provenance.
Exports include screenshots, model JSON, structure CSV, an offline HTML viewer, a conceptual IFC4 package and an audit pack.
features: Parses Primavera XER and P6 XML, XLSX, CSV and TSV schedules up to 4 GiB
Column mapping screen for unrecognised spreadsheet headings
Multi-file, multi-project programmes that never merge projects
Programme mode with project lanes, a paged activity film and cross-project logic
Combined 3D programme scene with one shared timeline
4D playback on planned, baseline, forecast or actual dates with lifecycle stage bars
Inspector with Activity, Coverage, Logic (P6 dependency register) and ALICE tabs
Element layers, work checklist, camera presets, engineering and realistic material styles
Library of 56 GLB element models across solar, wind, BESS, water, power, roads, rail and more
Conceptual IFC4 package export and a full audit pack with evidence and mappings
Built-in guided demo that runs the real pipeline on bundled synthetic samples
ai: No LLM or external model is used; the app runs fully offline.
A deterministic rule-based semantic classifier reads activity names and WBS paths to recognise industry, discipline and physical scope.
Industry layout rules choose representative element primitives and record the rule and confidence for each one in the inspector.
Uncertain decisions go into a review queue rather than being hidden (Autopilot or Review-gated modes).

stack.data: Local files and SQLite job/model cache; openpyxl, defusedxml, pypdf for ingest
stack.deploy: Local loopback app via scripts/task.py; Replit workflow on port 5000

screens.title: Upload
screens.caption: The start screen. Choose a schedule or a project package, add other schedules or documents, pick Autopilot or Review-gated, or run the guided demo.

screens.title: Column mapping
screens.caption: A CSV with non-standard headings opens this mapping screen. You map source columns to activity ID, name, WBS and planned dates before generation.

screens.title: Project chooser
screens.caption: Two sample files parsed into one programme of three separate projects. Open programme mode, the combined 3D programme, or a single project.

screens.title: Programme mode
screens.caption: Project lanes with activity counts and date windows, a programme timeline you can play, and the cross-project logic register.

screens.title: Combined 3D programme
screens.caption: All projects in one 3D scene with one timeline, here mid-playback. Element layers, the work checklist and lifecycle bars update as the date moves.

screens.title: Project model
screens.caption: The Water Treatment Demonstrator sample with panels cleared. The basin and clarifier equipment are representative elements derived from the schedule.

screens.title: Component inspector
screens.caption: Clicking an element opens the inspector with its source asset, the layout rule that placed it and why it is not a surveyed position.

screens.title: Coverage
screens.caption: The Coverage tab lists how many activities each project contributes to onsite geometry and which stay on the timeline only.

screens.title: 4D timeline and logic
screens.caption: Timeline playback with lifecycle stages next to the P6 dependency register from the Logic tab.

run:
python scripts/task.py bootstrap
python scripts/task.py start   # serves http://127.0.0.1:8765
notes: Ran locally from the repo (FastAPI + built React frontend) on a local port. All screens use the repo's bundled synthetic samples (samples/sample-multi-project.csv, sample-p6.xml, sample-mapping.csv) and its built-in guided demo; nothing was mocked. The frontend lockfile points at an unreachable Replit-internal npm mirror, so dependencies were installed from package.json ranges against the public registry without changing the lockfile. The video is the real walkthrough played back at 1.4x speed. The repo is a sanitized development snapshot, and its renderer uses schematic defaults rather than engineering geometry.
